items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: In a liner note Leonard Feather did some time ago for an album that Sonny Rollins didn't finish out... and we had done some things... Just recording things in there.

ctx.x: Yeah. Later on, I found out that John Coltrane and Jimmy Heath and Jackie McLean and Sonny Rollins and a lot of other guys had been studying me from out here. Milt Jackson, Percy Heath, all those guys could sing those solos note-for-note, and I couldn't even sing them! [LAUGHS HEARTILY]

But before we get too far, I'd like to go back a little ways and talk about my first professional recording. It was with Howard McGhee's group, the original group, and we did a recording for a little record store back behind the Civic Hotel, where I was living at the time. They started their own record label. They were doing the little pressing; they had one pressing machine -- they were doing a whole one-man
